rv.q: A brilliant spy thriller, a brilliant comedy, and a brilliant musical all rolled into one, it is exhilarating to see it hit the West End.

The talent was immediately apparent: nimbly varied, expressive music, ranging from sea shanty, to jazz to hip-hop; lyrics so patteringly exact and ingeniously rhymed that Noël Coward might have flushed with envy.
The gag rate is breathtaking and the songs are bangers.
Mission very much accomplished.
The show is witty, mocking, camp and joyous, not to mention immensely tuneful – the songs are both clever and catchy.
A West End run is the ultimate proof of concept for this irrepressible musical comedy, and the ingenious ensemble who created and perform it.
This would have been a five-star review had there not been a slight dimming of energy in an overextended second half.
This show could be just what the West End needs.
Really, it's a delight from start to finish.
I’d wager, all the same, that this inventive gem of a night is in with a very good fighting chance of resounding victory.
If you see one musical this year, make that Operation Mincemeat, the unlikely diamond of the West End.

So too does this boundlessly inventive show constantly set its ambitions seemingly beyond its resources (including a cast of five summoning numerous characters) — and somehow not just meet but exceed them.
It’s guaranteed to give your ability to grin and giggle a strenuous, much needed workout.
Operation Mincemeat is pure joy from start to finish, and a wonderfully unique addition to the West End.
This is one of those rare gems – a truly fantastic British musical that is sure to stand the test of time.
The show is a riot of wonderful moments and quite irresistible.
SpitLip are creative geniuses – their historically hilarious show will undoubtedly have a long, successful future ahead of it, some musicals are born to follow, this one is definitely born to lead.
Beautiful, frivolous and hugely entertaining
The aim may have been to make a dumb musical but there is nothing dumb about this cleverly written and flawlessly executed production.
It is a breath of fresh air to find this spirit in a world where more expensive, anxiously spectacular musicals too often turn out far, far duller.
This show should be on prescription!
If there's one show to see this year, make it Operation Mincemeat; if there are two, make it Operation Mincemeat twice
This show was already a major triumph, now it is sheer perfection.
Mission Complete: Operation Mincemeat is the wittiest, most exciting, and most fun show in the West End right now.

cn.t: Critics hail this scrappy British musical as a triumphant underdog success story, praising its inventive staging, brilliant five-person ensemble, and skillful tonal shifts from anarchic comedy to genuine emotion.
